A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LASER and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 7–13. Their corresponding content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LASER experiments on depth estimation, camera poses, and point-map reconstruction, including efficiency measurements and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds an overlap-size sensitivity experiment in supplementary Figure 9.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 7 and Algorithm 1 retain the same sliding-window reconstruction, IRLS/Kabsch registration, and layer-wise scale propagation. Incorporating appearance information is proposed only as future work, not as an implemented component.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained. The new overlap experiment reuses Sintel and Bonn for depth estimation and Sintel and ScanNet for pose estimation; it adds no new domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in corresponding tables and qualitative comparisons, including VGGT-Long and π3-Long in Tables 3 and 7. The new overlap experiment compares parameter settings of LASER.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation at overlap sizes O = 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10 in Figure 9. This extends the experimental settings through a parameter sweep; the previously reported benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary Figure 9 adds overlap-size sensitivity analysis alongside the existing window-size, IoU-threshold, and component ablations. Earlier registration analyses and failure-case images are retained rather than replaced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new overlap curves add no uncertainty estimates or changes to statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 9 newly reports Sintel/Bonn Abs Rel and Sintel/ScanNet ATE across overlap settings, showing relatively stable depth errors and variation in pose errors. Numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and earlier qualitative results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the layer-graph definitions, and mathematical objectives are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free streaming conversion, layer-wise alignment, reconstruction performance, and efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes streaming depth degradation to limited temporal context. Section 13 adds specific limitations: depth-only layers can merge distinct objects and lose correspondence after complete occlusion. Section 9 also interprets the overlap sweep as supporting the default accuracy–complexity tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies O = 5 as the default overlap in Figure 9 and Section 9; v1 reported overlap 5 in its runtime setup without that explicit default designation. Other implementation, hardware, preprocessing, timing, and project-access information is retained.

R1.justification: The same 73 references and research positioning are retained. Changes to reference page backlinks do not add cited works or alter relationships to prior methods.

P1.justification: v2 adds short explanatory passages in Sections 4.2 and 9 and a third future-direction bullet in Section 13. The section order and existing narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel overlap plot as Figure 9, renumbers the former Figures 9–11 to 10–12, adds page numbers, and reflows text. Existing displays are retained. The new plot misleadingly labels its default-overlap marker as 'Default Window Size'.

improvement.justification: The added overlap experiment provides limited supporting evidence for a practical parameter choice, while the new occlusion and object-separation limitations clarify LASER's applicability. These modest gains outweigh the new plot's small legend error. The method and principal benchmark results remain unchanged.
